entities.name: Battle of Ramree Island
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Ramree Island was a pivotal amphibious assault during World War II that took place on the island of Ramree in the Andaman Sea, off the coast of Burma in January 1945. The battle was a brutal and bloody conflict between the Imperial Japanese Army and the British Indian Army, resulting in the deaths of over 1,000 Japanese soldiers and an estimated 10,000–20,000 Allied casualties. The battle marked a turning point in the Burma Campaign, as the Allies gained control of the island and the surrounding waters, paving the way for the eventual defeat of the Japanese forces in the region.

The assault began on 18 January 1945, when a British Indian Army force landed on the western coast of the island, and quickly gained control of the surrounding beaches. However, the Japanese forces, who were well-entrenched in the island's interior, put up fierce resistance, and the battle raged on for several weeks. The Allies eventually gained the upper hand, but not before the Japanese forces had inflicted heavy casualties on the British Indian Army.

The Battle of Ramree Island had significant consequences, as it marked a turning point in the Burma Campaign. The Allies' victory on the island allowed them to control the surrounding waters and the Andaman Sea, which in turn enabled them to launch further attacks on the Japanese forces in the region. The battle also marked the beginning of the end of Japanese control in Burma, as the Allies continued to press their advantage in the region.

As one historian noted, 'The Battle of Ramree Island was a bloody and brutal conflict that marked a turning point in the Burma Campaign. The Allies' victory on the island paved the way for the eventual defeat of the Japanese forces in the region, and had significant consequences for the course of World War II.'
